pr_comments: @Kumataro Thanks a lot for the contribution! I hide the function implementation in cpp file and got rid of exceptions that are thrown outside of the function. The current image i/o contract is to be exception-safe and return bool status.
Yes, I changed the implementation that makes code exception safe. I propose to tune tests to handle status.
Thank you for your comment, and I fixed to use status code instead of catching exception.

issue_context.title: cv::imencode function fails writing vector<Mat>

review_comments: i think all encoders supports CV_8U so imho no need to this check

> i think all encoders supports CV_8U so imho no need to this check

Currently almost encoders supports CV_8U, but OpenEXR supports only CV_32F. And I think keeping behaviour between `imwrite()` and `imencode()` makes easy to debug encoders for current and future.

https://docs.opencv.org/4.10.0/d4/da8/group__imgcodecs.html#ga8ac397bd09e48851665edbe12aa28f25

> With OpenEXR encoder, only 32-bit float (CV_32F) images can be saved.
> 8-bit unsigned (CV_8U) images are not supported.

https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/450e741f8d53ff12b4e194c7762adaefb952555a/modules/imgcodecs/src/grfmt_exr.cpp#L697-L700

Thank you and I reconsider it, I updated it with some suggestion.

It is better that this fallback do not be processed if selected encoder doesn't supports CV_8U (Maybe only OpenEXR encoder). 

If only removing CV_Assert, ExrEncoder::write() may receive a non supported depth image which is not from User Application. So I think it makes small complex for Encoder debugging.

i think imwritemulti() also be defined as CV_EXPORTS_W and needs documentation

```
>>> help(cv2.imwritemulti)
Help on built-in function imwritemulti:

imwritemulti(...)
    imwritemulti(filename, img[, params]) -> retval
    .
```

Thank you for your comment ! I mistakenly thought that it was enough to support multiple images for imencode().

But it seems that encoding multiple images requests reading callback function. After appending it, it works well.
